correctness.rationale: The linearly non-degenerate transcendental curve has order 0<=rho<1 and normalized reduced entire coordinates y_j of order <=rho, as in Eremenko–Zhang Lemma 6.5. Their Corollary 6.3 gives H_y(r)<=n log+ r+r integral_0^infty N_y(t)/(r+t)^2 dt. If limsup N_1/T <1/J(rho), choose c strictly between and any a>1, alpha>rho, then transfer the Wronskian count to N_y(t)<=cH_y(a t)+C. The maximizing radii of H_y(r)/r^alpha satisfy integral <=I(alpha,a)H_y(r), where I(alpha,a)=integral max(1,(a u)^alpha)/(1+u)^2 du and I(alpha,a)->J(rho) as a down to1 and alpha down to rho. Choosing cI<1 bounds H_y(r_nu) by n log r_nu/(1-cI)+O(1). Cauchy estimates at this unbounded radius sequence force all coordinate Taylor coefficients above a finite degree to vanish; hence f is rational, a contradiction. At rho=0 J=1 recovers the primary bound, and at rho=1/2 J=1+pi/4 gives 4/(4+pi). Check alpha<1, normalized Wronskian nonzero, and that finite-order assumptions are on ordinary order, not merely lower order. No finite computation is used to infer the general theorem.
